mitigacoes.descricao: Encapsular o método Java 8 nas tags <Java> e </Java> para separar o prompt do código, melhorar a consistência da saída e reduzir texto errôneo na resposta; efeito não medido.

Construção de conjunto revisado com lista de palavras-chave ampliada e sem termos ambíguos, para reduzir falsos positivos, ruído e desbalanceamento do conjunto bruto; não há comparação do efeito sobre os resultados do modelo.
Omissão das 5 funções sem dataflow match score das médias da Table 2, para não distorcer os escores, conforme recomendação do CodeBLEU.

citacoes.trecho: We build a benchmark to evaluate large language models (LLMs) for source code migration tasks, specifically upgrading functions from Java 8 to Java 11.
We used a standardised role-based prompt in all of our experiments.

"You are a senior Java engineer. Convert Java 8 code to Java 11 while preserving behavior." "Change any syntax in the Java 8 code that was removed or deprecated by Java 11." "Output ONLY the Java 11 method."
We encapsulated the Java 8 function in "<Java>" and "</Java>" elements to create a clear structural boundary between the prompt and the code.
We intentionally evaluate a single-shot prompt, where the LLM is prompted once per function without ant iterative feedback or refinement.
A key limitation of this study is the absence of test execution or runtime validation.
citacoes.localizador: p. 6 do PDF, seção 6, «Threats to Internal Validity»

citacoes.trecho: While these metrics provide useful insights into lexical, syntactic, and structural changes introduced during migration, they cannot guarantee compilation success or functional equivalence.
This is important as if a deprecated keyword is still present in the generated Java 11 code, the code would fail to compile and would be principally incorrect.
This change would make the "isp" list immutable when it was previously a mutable list.
However, the use of a single LLM limits the findings to Codestral.
citacoes.localizador: p. 6 do PDF, seção 6, «Threats to External Validity»

citacoes.trecho: Although the dataset was synthetic and thus not directly reflective of real-world codebases, it provided a cleaner and more controlled benchmark for assessing LLMs' ability to detect, update, and preserve functionality during Java version migration.
5 functions had no dataflow match scores and were omitted to prevent skewing the scores (as recommended by codebleu).
40% of the functions had all keywords removed, however, only 31.82% of the 66 keywords used in the dataset were successfully removed.
